stem: A well-known environmental slogan encourages people to first cut down on unnecessary consumption, then use items multiple times, and finally process used materials into new products, in that order of preference. This principle is known as the:
explanation: The 3 R's — Reduce (use less in the first place), Reuse (use items again before discarding), Recycle (process waste into new materials) — are listed in order of environmental preference, since reducing consumption has the greatest impact, recycling the least (though still valuable).

stem: Kitchen waste like vegetable peels and dry leaves can be piled together and left to naturally decompose (with the help of microorganisms and earthworms) into a nutrient-rich material used to fertilise soil. This process is called:
explanation: Composting uses decomposers (bacteria, fungi, earthworms) to break down organic waste into nutrient-rich humus, an eco-friendly alternative to chemical fertilisers — distinct from fermentation (converting sugars via microbes, as in bread/curd) or distillation (physical separation by boiling point).
